name: Bentong
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Only survey/classification refs (Grimes & Grimes 1987 survey; Smith 2017); no phonological description found.

sources.citation: Friberg, Timothy & Barbara Friberg. 1991. Notes on Konjo phonology. In J.N. Sneddon (ed.), Studies in Sulawesi linguistics, part II (NUSA 33), 71-115.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: NOT a Bentong source: nearest-relative proxy only (Konjo, 77% lexical similarity). Gives penultimate-stress rules for the Makassaric neighbour; useful solely as family context if the catalog ever records proxies.

Segmental inventory only (6 vowels, 15 consonants, NC clusters, geminates /kk ll mm nn pp rr ss/, sound correspondences vs. standard Bugis, labialization/palatalization) for the Dentong variety of Kec. Cenrana, Kab. Maros; no section or remark on stress, accent, or suprasegmentals (a full-text search for stress/accent and read).

sources.citation: Jukes, Anthony. 2006. Makassarese (basa Mangkasara'): a description of an Austronesian language of South Sulawesi. PhD thesis, University of Melbourne (text held under catalog maka1311).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Phonology chapter concerns Gowa Makassarese only; Bentong appears solely in the classification discussion (sec. 1.2.2, fn. 19: Jukes could not personally confirm the language's existence). Nothing on Bentong stress.

sources.citation: Friberg, Timothy & Thomas V. Laskowske. 1989. South Sulawesi languages, 1989. In J.N. Sneddon (ed.), Studies in Sulawesi linguistics, part 1 (NUSA 31), 1-17. Jakarta: Universitas Katolik Atma Jaya. http://sealang.net/archives/nusa/pdf/nusa-v31-p1-18.pdf (no text layer; scanned at 300 dpi).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Lexicostatistical survey update; p.3 adds 'Bentong or Dentong' as a fifth Makasar-family language (75% with Makasar (Lakiung), 77% Highland Konjo) located where Makasar, Bugis and Highland Konjo meet; announces an SIL Makasar survey report that apparently never appeared.

sources.citation: Grimes, Charles E. & Barbara D. Grimes. 1987. Languages of South Sulawesi. Pacific Linguistics D-78. Canberra: ANU. (only Glottolog ref for bent1237; held)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No Bentong data at all (the Bentong area is mapped as Konjo; Bentong was first split off by Friberg & Laskowske 1989). Only a family-wide remark in the Appendix E symbol key, printed p.94: 'Stress in South Sulawesi languages usually occurs on the penultimate syllable. In such cases it is not marked in the word lists.' (p.96 notes antepenultimate exceptions for Selayar).
